validity.researcher_notes: SOURCE-OF-RECORD IDENTIFIED. The row's sole wiki citation is 'OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2017, page 134' (4 backlinks). I retrieved the real PDF via the Wayback Machine and confirmed page 133->134 Table 9.9 ('Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016'). Under Iraq it lists verbatim: 'Trans-Iraqi dry gas pipeline/Najaf PWR St | OPC | 74 (miles) | 24 (inches)'. So this is NOT a phantom GEM invention -- a credible source (Iraq data reported to OPEC) names it explicitly with exactly the GEM values. EXISTENCE: real per OPEC ASB, and independently the destination facility exists (Najaf gas-fired power station, ~375-495 MW; power-technology.com) and the southern Iraqi dry-gas transmission network reaching Najaf/Hilla/Diwaniyah power stations is independently documented (rawabetcenter history of Iraqi gas; Samawa CCGT ESIA references the existing 24-inch North Rumaila-Samawa dry-gas trunk feeding these plants). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- a 74-mile, 24-inch DRY-GAS TRANSMISSION spur off the Trans-Iraq dry-gas trunk to a power station; it is gas (not one of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines) and not plant-internal. DUPLICATE CHECK: NOT a duplicate. OPEC Table 9.9 separately lists 'Strategic pipeline/Al-Najaf PWR St | OPC | 23 mi | 16 in' (= GEM P1848 Strategic-Najaf, 37 km/16 in). P4064 and P1848 both terminate at Najaf PWR St but tap DIFFERENT trunks (Trans-Iraq dry-gas vs the Strategic pipeline) and differ in length (74 vs 23 mi) and diameter (24 vs 16 in) -- two distinct physical feeders, not one line double-counted. P4064 is also distinct from its siblings P4062 (Hilla, 25/24), P4065 (Dewania, 50/24), P4066 (Daura, 29/18), each a different Table 9.9 row. CAVEAT: single aggregate source; no SECOND independent source names or specs this exact line, and that source is now link-rotted (live opec.org PDF URL redirects to the OPEC homepage -- url_verifier returns a spurious 200 because 'Iraq' appears in the site nav). tier=medium.

routes.corridor_desc: Per OPEC ASB 2017 Table 9.9 the line runs from the Trans-Iraq dry-gas trunk to Najaf power station, length 74 miles (~119 km). The trunk is the north-south southern-Iraq dry-gas network (Rumaila/North Rumaila -> Nasiriyah -> Samawa -> Diwaniyah -> Najaf/Hilla -> Baghdad; documented in the rawabetcenter history and the Samawa CCGT ESIA's '24-inch North Rumaila-Samawa' reference). A 74-mile spur puts the trunk junction ~near Samawa, with the line running NW up the Euphrates corridor via the Diwaniyah area to the Najaf power station. LOOSE BOUND: only the end facility (Najaf power station) is firmly located; the trunk tap is unlocated, so the corridor is bounded, not surveyed.
routes.researcher_notes: End coordinate is APPROXIMATE, defensible from the named place Najaf (city ~31.99N,44.33E; the gas power station sits in the Najaf/Abbasiya area just E/SE of the city) -- I did NOT cite a GEM/Google-Maps plant coordinate. Start (trunk tap) coordinate left null because it cannot be sourced; Samawah and Diwaniyah city coordinates are given only as loose corridor waypoints (well-known city locations), not as pipeline points. No coordinate was fabricated. Corridor is a bounded suggestion for a later human routes-repo branch, never an auto-applied route.
